changes.event: A (fictional) state appellate court held a retailer liable for refund promises
changes.event_description: A state appellate court (the item marks it as fictional, a manually entered demo) held a retailer liable for refund promises its customer-service chatbot made. The court rejected the defense that the chatbot was a separate agent responsible for its own statements, and it let affected customers pursue their claims together as a group.
changes.reasoning: This is directly on point for unauthorized_commitment. Liability for chatbot promises is already reflected in the prior through the Moffatt v. Air Canada reference, so the new element is that group claims were allowed. A systematic chatbot promise made to many customers can now aggregate into a group claim. That points to a higher share of claims becoming group claims, so I propose a +30% change to tail.prob. A possible secondary effect is a higher p_claim_given_harm, but only one parameter can be moved and the group-claim holding is the more novel signal. An appellate ruling would normally rate as strong. I rated it moderate because the item is labeled fictional or demo, comes from a single jurisdiction, and gives no loss figures.

changes.event: Code to Deploy Destructive AI Agent Discovered in Amazon Q VS Code Extension
changes.event_description: Malicious code inserted into an official Amazon Q VS Code extension release instructed the AI agent to wipe local and cloud resources. The release was later revoked.
changes.reasoning: This is a real provider-level compromise that shipped to many users at once, which is a precursor of a systemic event. No widespread losses were reported, so it supports only a slight upward nudge.

changes.event: Data Destruction via Indirect Prompt Injection Targeting Claude Computer-Use
changes.event_description: HiddenLayer researchers hid a prompt injection in a PDF. When Claude Computer Use opened the file, it ran a shell command that wiped the filesystem.
changes.reasoning: A research demonstration with no real victim. It shows that agentic tool access lets a successful injection cause destructive loss, which supports a small upward nudge to the share of injections that cause harm.

changes.event: Data Exfiltration from Slack AI via Indirect Prompt Injection
changes.event_description: PromptArmor showed that a malicious post in a public Slack channel could make Slack AI leak private data, such as an API key, to an attacker.
changes.reasoning: A demonstration with no reported loss. It shows a realistic exfiltration path through retrieval-based assistants, so at most a weak signal.

changes.event: Financial Transaction Hijacking with M365 Copilot as an Insider
changes.event_description: Zenity researchers sent a crafted email that made Microsoft 365 Copilot give a user the attacker's bank details for a wire transfer.
changes.reasoning: A red-team exercise with no actual fraud loss. It is consistent with injection leading to financial fraud, so a weak upward signal.
